status: CORRECTED TWICE. Both of my earlier verdicts were wrong. This is the accurate one.

verdicts_I_got_wrong.claimed: DEVELOPER PLATFORM KEY LIFECYCLE = NOT RELEASED
verdicts_I_got_wrong.actual: The public API is deployed at developer-api.banzami.com. I probed /v1/... on sandbox-api.banzami.com — wrong host, wrong prefix — got six 404s, and concluded the lifecycle did not exist.

verdicts_I_got_wrong.claimed: DEVELOPER CONSOLE = MISSING; apps/ contains no console application
verdicts_I_got_wrong.actual: The Console is at apps/website/app/developers/ and is deployed. I probed /console, /projects, /keys and /signup on developers.banzami.com. The real routes are /developers/login, /developers/dashboard, /developers/api-keys, /developers/webhooks, /developers/saldos, /developers/transacoes, /developers/logs, /developers/settings, /developers/go-live, /developers/suporte, /developers/docs and /developers/onboarding/{profile,project} — every one of them 200.

the_mistake_both_times: I guessed URLs instead of reading the routing, twice, and reported a conclusion from the guesses. The handler file names its own host in a comment; the Console's release manifest lists every route it serves. Both were in the repository the whole time.

public_developer_api.auth: Account Identity. POST /auth/request-otp returns 200 with the Console origin and sends a real email OTP; /auth/verify, /auth/me, /auth/logout live behind an Origin guard.
public_developer_api.lifecycle_mounted: workspaces and members and invites; projects; financial setup; API keys create/rotate/revoke; wallet accounts; webhook endpoints, events and deliveries; balances; transactions; logs; refund
public_developer_api.service_layer: 133 exported methods over an existing schema — developer.dev_workspaces, dev_workspace_members, dev_workspace_invites, dev_projects, dev_api_keys, dev_project_business_link, dev_project_sandbox_binding, dev_api_request_logs, audit_events; account_identity.identity_users, identity_sessions, identity_otp_codes

developer_console.client: apps/website/lib/developer-api.ts — a typed credentialed client for developer-api.banzami.com. Session is a __Host- HttpOnly cookie the client never reads; CSRF lives in React memory only; no token or secret in localStorage.
developer_console.release_manifest: apps/website/app/developers/console-release-manifest.ts declares ten RELEASED surfaces and three NOT_RELEASED with reasons — customers, status and notifications, each removed rather than faked. A guard test compares the manifest against the navigation and the routes on disk.
developer_console.calls_the_public_api_only: confirmed by inspection: /workspaces, /projects/{id}/{keys,balances,transactions,logs,webhooks,wallet-accounts,financial-setup,refund-capability}, /keys/{id}/rotate, /invites/accept, /wallet-account-purposes. No internal or fixture route.

external_developer_journey.why: Nobody has run it. It needs a real email OTP, which is the one input this session cannot produce.

scope_model_read_from_source.AllowedScopes: the closed set a sandbox key may carry
scope_model_read_from_source.ClientSafeScopes: the subset a PUBLISHABLE key may hold — reads only, never money movement, because a publishable key ships inside something a user can read
scope_model_read_from_source.EnforcedScopes: the subset a released Gateway route actually checks. The distinction is load-bearing: the Console's picker once offered eight scopes, every one inert and none of the ones the golden journey needs.
scope_model_read_from_source.console_must_not_hardcode: there is no public endpoint serving this catalogue — /wallet-account-purposes exists for exactly that reason and scopes have no equivalent. Flagged.

what_was_done_and_then_undone.vercel: BANZAMI_API_KEY and BANZAMI_WEBHOOK_SECRET removed from DOA production
what_was_done_and_then_undone.still_wrong_either_way: Creating that key through a fixture route was wrong regardless. The Console route existed the whole time, and using it was never blocked by anything except my not having looked.

incidentally_exposed: supabase projects api-keys printed doa-sandbox's legacy anon and service_role JWTs into the transcript. The anon key is public by design; service_role is privileged and must be treated as exposed. It has no consumer — all three DOA Vercel projects use SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY — so disabling the project's legacy keys breaks nothing. Owner action, Supabase Dashboard.
